description: Clause cases merged from the clause-case files of carve-js, carve-php and carve-rs (next2), each kept only where a clause decides it; why quotes the deciding sentence. Curated by hand. See README.md.

cases.why: C2-B-130: A line of a line block keeps the spaces that lead it after the strip (C2-B-027) as content (carried over from 0.1).
cases.summary: indented line block keeps leading space

cases.why: C2-B-130: A line of a line block keeps the spaces that lead it after the strip (C2-B-027) as content (carried over from 0.1). C2-B-123: The body of a line block is one leaf that recognizes only prefixes and the closer: every other line is a line of text.
cases.summary: line block in quote in item keeps tab

cases.why: C2-B-119: Behind those spaces a sigil starts a sigil div also when further words are glued to it, and C2-B-122 reports the words: `::: >a` opens a quote fence.
cases.summary: sigil with glued words opens empty line block

cases.why: C2-B-225: Where it is not a space, a brace block there is an attribute block (C2-B-105) and any other character starts further words (C2-B-122).
cases.summary: attribute block glued to div name not applied

cases.why: C2-H-166: For `max_nesting` the children of the document stand at level 0, and each block level and each inline level below adds one. A node at a level above the bound is outside the profile; a node at the bound stays, and its children are degraded.
cases.summary: comment profile nesting bound degrades code span

cases.why: C2-H-165: every other inline node with no children as the writer spells that node on its own (C2-W-116), since a tree holds no source text.
cases.summary: comment profile degrades inline math to source spelling

cases.why: C2-A-084: Its panels are the tables among its children, and the image paragraphs, code blocks, quotes and math blocks among them that carry a caption; there is no separate panel list.
cases.summary: nested figure group is no panel, caption numbered

cases.why: C2-A-049: It carries `format`, which is the word on its opener or `"yaml"` when there is none, and `value`, the text between the delimiters as written, which ends with a line break after its last line also where the block is unclosed and the source ends there without one (C2-A-046).
cases.summary: unclosed frontmatter keeps trailing whitespace line

cases.why: C2-B-171: A cell prefix is the optional header cell mark `|=`, then an optional run of glued brace blocks, merged into one (C2-B-093). C2-I-034: One part that fits no shape makes the whole run no attribute block.
cases.summary: cell prefix stops at invalid brace block

cases.why: C2-B-225: The first character behind the run that is not one of them ends the run; it is part of no name.
cases.summary: figure name with glued words gives figure group

cases.why: C2-B-043: A bare dot is no marker when the text behind its required space starts with another dot and a space, so `. . . and then silence` is a paragraph.
cases.summary: bare dot before spaced dot is text

cases.why: C2-H-165: A node that leaves no text is dropped.
cases.summary: minimal profile drops empty degraded table

cases.why: C2-I-076: A reference label is the run of characters up to the next `]` that no backslash escapes.
cases.summary: label ends at first bracket, no block image

cases.why: C2-I-079: A label whose key is empty after folding, one that holds only spaces, tabs or a line break, is no label: the brackets are text.
cases.summary: blank image label is text, no caption

cases.why: C2-I-078: A label whose first character is an at-sign is not a reference label. C2-I-101: The brackets are text and the key is read as a mention (C2-I-078, C2-I-090).
cases.summary: at-sign label is no reference, mention

cases.why: C2-I-077: Atoms are read first, so a line comment that starts inside a label takes the rest of its line (C2-I-024): the label is unclosed and the brackets are text.
cases.summary: line comment in image label, no image

cases.why: C2-I-024: A line comment takes the rest of its line with every closer on it.
cases.summary: line comment in image alt, no image

cases.why:
C2-B-197: A block image line is decided by its shape and not by inline parsing: the line consists of exactly one image form, `![alt](destination)`, `![alt][label]` or the collapsed `![alt][]`, optional attribute blocks glued to it (C2-I-039), and trailing spaces. C2-H-020: Where the image is an unresolved reference, C2-H-085 writes it as text, and text needs a block around it: the paragraph then keeps its `

`.
cases.summary: unresolved block image with caption keeps p

cases.why: C2-I-069: A tail with a space in the destination, a broken title or a line break is no tail: the bracket pair is text and the parenthesis is text.
cases.summary: tab after title breaks image tail

cases.why: C2-B-122: An unquoted title or further words in the info string do not stop the block from opening, and `fence-title-syntax` reports them.
cases.summary: spaced brace block after figure ignored

cases.why: C2-H-024: Authored ids are reserved first, in document order. Generated ids follow in document order, and a slug that is already taken gets the suffix `-2`, then `-3`, and so on.
cases.summary: id on unresolved reference reserves slug

cases.why: C2-I-033: A quoted value stands in `"` or `'`.
cases.summary: single-quoted value holding double quote

cases.why:
C2-H-020: Where the image is an unresolved reference, C2-H-085 writes it as text, and text needs a block around it: the paragraph then keeps its `

`.
cases.summary: unresolved block image keeps paragraph

cases.why: C2-B-084: Exactly one space separates the colon from the expansion: every character after it belongs to the expansion, a leading space or tab included, except the spaces and tabs at the end of the line.
cases.summary: abbreviation expansion keeps second space

cases.why: C2-I-118: An opener read while 200 entries are open is text: it is not pushed and takes part in no pairing, and the scan goes on behind it.
cases.summary: inline footnote opener past depth 200

cases.why: C2-I-118: An opener read while 200 entries are open is text: it is not pushed and takes part in no pairing, and the scan goes on behind it.
cases.summary: bracket inside extension past depth 200

cases.why: C2-H-165: Inside a block that is degraded as a whole, the plain text is that of C2-H-143 for every node except an image, which keeps `[img: ALT]`, so a `code`, a `literal_inline` and a `math` node give their value.
cases.summary: minimal profile degrades quote to marked plain text

cases.why: C2-I-118: Inline nesting stops at depth 200 in each inline content, whatever the blocks around it: the count starts at zero where the content starts (C2-I-120), and no block counts (C2-B-190).
cases.summary: inline depth ignores 199 open blocks

cases.why: C2-B-154: A line that is not indented past the marker starts a new block; a comment-only line is no such line (C2-B-137), so its comment is a child of the heading (C2-B-138) and an indented line below it still continues the heading.
cases.summary: comment-only line below heading joins heading

cases.why: C2-B-184: Each fragment is an inline content by itself (C2-B-223), so every inline form opens and closes inside one physical row, and an opener whose closer is not in its own fragment is text, as at the end of a cell.
cases.summary: emphasis cannot span continuation row fragments

cases.why: C2-I-104: A quote opens when the neighbor before it is whitespace or opening punctuation, or when it has none because the quote stands at the start of the content or directly behind an opening mark or bracket. Otherwise it closes, also directly behind a closing mark, a closing bracket or an atom.
cases.summary: smart quotes read from neighbors, apostrophe before digit

cases.why: C2-H-133: It renders as a paragraph that holds the directive as text: `{{`, a space, the path as C2-H-171 writes it, the section, the options in the order of C2-W-058 and the entries of `invalid` as the tree holds them, each after one space, a space and `}}`.
cases.summary: unexpanded include keeps invalid options as written

cases.why: C2-B-172: A `<` in the first column, a `<` whose left cell is covered by a row span from above, a `^` in the first row of its group and a `^` below a cell that spans more than one column join nothing (C2-B-173): in `|a|<|` above `|^|b|`, the `^` is the text of its cell.
cases.summary: span mark at first row of body and foot

cases.why: C2-B-209: A count larger than the number of rows is the number of rows, so every row is in the head, and `table-row-count-clamped` reports the count.
cases.summary: delimited table header-rows clamped to row count

cases.why: C2-H-063: The `attrs`, `lang` and `dir` of such a block are written on its `
cases.summary: captioned image attributes move to figure

cases.why: C2-A-082: Below a code block, which holds no children, it is the sibling after the block (C2-A-145).
cases.summary: comment between code block and caption

cases.why: C2-B-138: The comment of a comment-only line, and a comment that stands alone after a marker or a quote mark, is a child of the open leaf when one is open, and otherwise a comment node of the innermost open container, whatever the line's indent.
cases.summary: comment between quote and its caption

cases.why: C2-H-096: A resolved cross-reference is `<a href="#ID">` around generated text. ... For a numbered caption it is the label word and the number, such as `Figure 1`.
cases.summary: xref to captioned math block id

expected.html: See Equation 1.

cases.why: C2-H-064: Each panel in it (C2-A-084) is `<figure class="carve-figure-panel">` in place of the `<figure>` of C2-H-062, and the caption of the group is the last child of the group. A table panel is wrapped too: the panel figure holds the `<table>`, which keeps its caption as `<caption>` (C2-H-061) and has no `<figcaption>`.
cases.summary: figure group with image and table panels
cases.input:
::: figure
![a](a.png)
^ (a) First

| t |
^ T
:::
^ Figure #: Both

cases.why: C2-H-019: A paragraph that holds only a braced comment is this case, and so is one of braced comments on several lines.
cases.summary: paragraph of two braced comments renders nothing

cases.why: C2-H-166: A node at a level above the bound is outside the profile; a node at the bound stays, and its children are degraded.
cases.summary: comment profile nesting bound at level 4

cases.why: C2-B-190: Block nesting stops at depth 200: each open quote, list, item, description list, description, footnote body and div counts one, and while 200 are open an opener of one more is text.
cases.summary: 200 quotes open, inline footnote unaffected

cases.why: C2-B-015: A marker left of every open list continues the outermost open list when its marker matches under C2-B-049 and the container that holds that list owns the line (C2-B-025); otherwise it closes the open lists and opens a new one, whatever its value, in the innermost container that owns the line (C2-B-228).
cases.summary: list marker at column 0 closes footnote list

cases.why: C2-I-013: A link destination reads only the escaped parenthesis and the escaped backslash.
cases.summary: definition destination decodes escaped backslash

cases.why: C2-I-013: A link destination reads only the escaped parenthesis and the escaped backslash.
cases.summary: definition destination decodes escaped parenthesis

cases.why: C2-H-166: A `list_item` counts a level but is never degraded on its own: it keeps its `<li>`, and its blocks are degraded.
cases.summary: minimal nesting bound in nested list

cases.why: C2-I-002: The test is lexical: a space behind an odd run of backslashes is kept, also inside a form that reads no escapes (C2-I-013).
cases.summary: escaped trailing space kept in code span

cases.why: C2-I-002: A tab behind a backslash is removed like any other tab at the end of a line.
cases.summary: trailing tab after backslash removed in code span

cases.why: C2-H-165: a `comment` and a `critic_comment` give no text, so a paragraph that holds only comments still writes nothing (C2-H-019);
cases.summary: minimal drops critic comment inline

cases.why: C2-B-084: Exactly one space separates the colon from the expansion: every character after it belongs to the expansion, a leading space or tab included, except the spaces and tabs at the end of the line.
cases.summary: abbreviation expansion keeps leading tab

cases.why: C2-H-051: The carrier is written for no other raw span: with `rawHtml` on a raw span with the format `html` is verbatim (C2-H-053), and a raw span in any other format renders nothing (C2-H-054), also under `roundtrip`.
cases.summary: raw html span verbatim under roundtrip with rawHtml on

cases.why: C2-H-051: The carrier is written for no other raw span: with `rawHtml` on a raw span with the format `html` is verbatim (C2-H-053), and a raw span in any other format renders nothing (C2-H-054), also under `roundtrip`.
cases.summary: latex raw span dropped under roundtrip

cases.why: C2-A-182: For `{{ a.crv }}` and two spaces the include spans offsets 0 to 13; indented by two spaces, with two spaces behind it, it spans 2 to 15.
cases.summary: include span covers trailing spaces, unexpanded render

cases.why: C2-A-182: For `{{ a.crv }}` and two spaces the include spans offsets 0 to 13; indented by two spaces, with two spaces behind it, it spans 2 to 15.
cases.summary: indented include with trailing spaces, span and render

cases.why: C2-A-086: For `| a |`, `%% x` and `+ b |` on three lines, the body holds the row `a b` and then the comment `x`, and the table holds no comment after its groups.
cases.summary: comment between a row and its continuation

cases.why: C2-A-086: A comment between a row and its continuation row (C2-B-175), as a comment-only line or as the trailing comment of the row, belongs to the row's group, directly after the row, because the continuation is part of that row (C2-B-184)
cases.summary: trailing row comment before continuation row placement

cases.why: C2-I-017: A backtick run with no closing run of its length later in the same content opens nothing (C2-I-119): the run is text, and so is a `!`, `$` or `$$` glued before it. The scan goes on behind the run, so a shorter or longer run after it may open a span.
cases.summary: unmatched backtick runs stay text

cases.why: C2-B-225: The first character behind the run that is not one of them ends the run; it is part of no name. Where it is not a space, a brace block there is an attribute block (C2-B-105) and any other character starts further words (C2-B-122).
cases.summary: div name ends at glued bracket, empty div

cases.why: C2-I-111: A run of two or more hyphens becomes dashes: a length divisible by three gives em dashes, otherwise a length divisible by two gives en dashes, otherwise one em dash followed by the rest under the same rule.
cases.summary: eight hyphens become four en dashes

cases.why: C2-B-033: Every marker needs one space and at least one further character on its line, so a bare marker and a marker without its space are text.
cases.summary: hyphen glued to insert span is no marker

cases.why: C2-B-206: An option is invalid when its key is not one of the six, when its value is outside the shape of its key, when it has no value and `data/include-options.json` needs one, or when its key stood earlier in the directive. An invalid option has no effect on the tree: the node keeps it as written (C2-A-181), `include-option-invalid` reports it, and the expansion leaves an include that holds one unexpanded (C2-N-025).
cases.summary: invalid include options kept and rendered as text

cases.why: C2-I-017: A backtick run with no closing run of its length later in the same content opens nothing (C2-I-119): the run is text, and so is a `!`, `$` or `$$` glued before it. The scan goes on behind the run, so a shorter or longer run after it may open a span.
cases.summary: unclosed code span text, scan continues to strong

cases.why: C2-I-104: A quote opens when the neighbor before it is whitespace or opening punctuation, or when it has none because the quote stands at the start of the content or directly behind an opening mark or bracket. Otherwise it closes, also directly behind a closing mark, a closing bracket or an atom.
cases.summary: nested single quotes read from neighbors only

cases.why: C2-I-017: A backtick run with no closing run of its length later in the same content opens nothing (C2-I-119): the run is text, and so is a `!`, `$` or `$$` glued before it.
cases.summary: unclosed literal-text span keeps bang as text

cases.why: C2-H-062: An image paragraph, a code block, a quote or a math block that carries a caption (C2-A-082) is written as `<figure>` around the block and then `<figcaption>` with the caption.
cases.summary: numbered caption on block image figure

cases.why: C2-H-166: A node at a level above the bound is outside the profile; a node at the bound stays, and its children are degraded. A `list_item` counts a level but is never degraded on its own: it keeps its `<li>`, and its blocks are degraded.
cases.summary: nested list source lines under minimal profile nesting

cases.why: C2-B-190: A marker that opens two containers at once, a list and its item or a description list and its first description, is tested as one: when both do not fit, the whole marker is text and neither opens.
cases.summary: list marker at block depth limit is text

cases.why: C2-B-173: A span mark that joins nothing is an ordinary cell that holds the mark as text, and `table-span-marker-blocked` reports it.
cases.summary: first-row span mark is text, row not head

cases.why: C2-H-062: An image paragraph, a code block, a quote or a math block that carries a caption (C2-A-082) is written as `<figure>` around the block and then `<figcaption>` with the caption.
cases.summary: captioned math block inside quote renders figure

cases.why: C2-B-148: A caption is paragraph-like: its text takes lazy lines and ends as a paragraph does, so a second caption line directly below a caption continues the first.
cases.summary: lazy caption line on empty nested quote

cases.why: C2-B-206: An option is invalid when its key is not one of the six, when its value is outside the shape of its key, when it has no value and `data/include-options.json` needs one, or when its key stood earlier in the directive.
cases.summary: repeated and malformed shift options invalid

cases.why: C2-I-053: A bare span that holds its own delimiter character between two word characters does not form: its entry leaves the stack, every other entry stays, and both delimiters are text.
cases.summary: braced comment transparent for inner delimiter test

cases.why: C2-B-166: A table row is a line that starts with a pipe after the prefixes and ends with a pipe, after which only a row attribute and a line comment may follow (C2-B-167), with at least two pipes, so a pipe alone on a line is text. C2-B-133: The line form is `%%` at the start of a line or after whitespace, it runs to the end of the line, and elsewhere `%%` is text.
cases.summary: percent run after row pipe is a trailing line comment
cases.corrected: the engine files expected row `| 1 | %%%` read as paragraph text `| 1 |` with a line comment; no body row

cases.why: C2-B-225: The first character behind the run that is not one of them ends the run; it is part of no name. Where it is not a space, a brace block there is an attribute block (C2-B-105) and any other character starts further words (C2-B-122).
cases.summary: tab after fence language starts further words

cases.why: C2-B-085: For a duplicate label the first definition wins, and `duplicate-footnote-definition`, `duplicate-link-reference-definition` or `duplicate-abbreviation-definition` reports the later one.
cases.summary: duplicate footnote kept in tree and resolved
